ranking_basis: Pre-implementation qualitative ranking by physical specificity, likely separation from named mimics, and cost. Sign and magnitude of DTI change are unmeasured; no score projection is made. Novelty against the full family registry is not established. Ranks 1-4 are the original same-lane block; ranks 5-9 are the new geological block (G-01..G-05), ranked against each other by expected improvement per unit cost. The two blocks are not compared numerically.

protocol.input_availability: The competition data page requires login in this session and the checkout has no official rasters or shared cached stack. USGS 3DEP provides public-domain 1 m bare-earth DEMs in principle, but exact competition-area tile coverage/alignment is not verified.
protocol.holdout: Withhold whole vector-defined fault segments, not artificial raster chunks, from lidar-covered spatial blocks. Use a preregistered spatial buffer around held segments; recommend matching the 300 m scoring support, subject to review by the two independent scientific leads. Catalogue-derived features use visible faults only; visible fault pixels are masked exactly. Restrict truth and scoring to lidar-covered held-out blocks.
protocol.metric: Pooled distance-weighted Tversky, alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, 300 m triangular kernel. Report evaluator version, withheld-positive count, and a 95% spatial-block CI for every HOLDOUT-DTI result.
protocol.leakage: Test every feature alone on the spatially blocked holdout. AUC >0.90 is leakage until disproven. No hidden/withheld catalogue data may affect features, masks, candidate eligibility, or thresholds.
protocol.range_front_gate: Compare gains in lidar-covered held-out blocks both overall and off a prespecified range-front stratum; reject a gain confined to range fronts.
protocol.uniqueness: Compare continuous pre-placement surfaces and final dots against the complete registry. Correlation >0.90 or >70% of candidate dots within 3 px is a duplicate/lane-drift stop. Incomplete registry means BLOCKED, not PASS.
protocol.budget: Maximum three experiments or two hours. No competition slot before the candidate strictly beats the current valid holdout best under the same protocol.

items.title: Slope-aware scarp templates plus scale-persistent Steger/Frangi line evidence
items.layers: Authorized 1 m bare-earth DEM tiles and the shared cached stack; Scarplet-style template outputs (best-fit amplitude, morphologic age, orientation, and template SNR); signed Steger sub-pixel ridge/valley responses and Frangi Hessian-line measures over 2–20 m scales; the existing cultural-feature mask only after its provenance, alignment, and availability are verified. Aggregate physical channel summaries to the competition's 100 m cells.
items.signature: A coherent scarp cross-profile fit that allows finite initial and far-field slopes, co-located with ridge/valley responses persisting across neighboring physical scales and aligned along a trace. Template amplitude, morphologic age, orientation, and SNR must be computed by the cited template method rather than approximated by ratios or robust z-scores.
items.why_off_catalogue: An expert-labelled new fault may preserve a subtle surface scarp omitted from the public compilation. Native DEM evidence can preserve profile shape and continuity that are diluted by coarser aggregation. This is a geological rationale to test, not an observed gain.
items.named_mimic: Fluvial terrace riser. Also test natural channel banks, road/canal embankments, landslide headscarps, shoreline risers, and DEM seams.
items.differs_from_repo: The present H66 code decodes owner-described 100 m stack proxies; it does not implement the actual Scarplet template fit or footprint-wide native Steger/Frangi scale sweep. Sibling owner reports describe LiDAR scarp channels and thinning, so the joined slope-aware template plus signed cross-scale line persistence is a candidate distinction, not a verified novelty claim. The full raster registry is unavailable.
items.cost: Very high: tiled DEM/projection and edge handling, multi-orientation and multiscale operators, mask validation, aggregation, per-feature leakage tests, segment-blocked holdout/CI, full-registry scans, and shared-tool corrections. Runtime and storage are unknown until exact tiles are inventoried.
items.expected_gain: Highest qualitative prior in this ranking because it combines two complementary physical measurements; sign and size are unknown. Not a DTI projection.
items.data_status: Blocked. Official competition rasters, tile list, shared cache, and existing cultural mask are absent. USGS 3DEP 1 m project DEMs are public domain in principle, but exact study-area coverage and compatibility are unverified (S04, S05, S07).
items.validation: NOT RUN. This is the lead to review before implementation. Do not emit a candidate until authorized data, corrected shared holdout/writer, complete registry, independent scientific sign-offs, and budget are available.
items.implementation_status: IMPLEMENTED as H67-1 (scarp-lane novelty field + density-equalizing systematic sampler). Outcome: 3 of 4 pre-registered predictions met, P3 measured FALSE (block-density CV 0.32 vs the 0.45-0.58 band), science gate UNEVALUABLE (IR-67-INSTR-01), format and lane checks pass with the IR-67-GATE-02 exception. Not promoted.

items.title: Slope-aware scarp-template channels alone
items.layers: The same authorized native DEM and shared cache; a template search over scarp orientation and morphologic age that estimates amplitude and template SNR while allowing nonzero regional slopes; aggregate amplitude, age, orientation, and SNR summaries to 100 m.
items.signature: Consistent cross-profile curvature/step fit with a stable orientation and plausible along-trace amplitude despite a dipping surface and unequal adjacent slopes.
items.why_off_catalogue: Small or gently dipping scarps may be missed by regional mapping and weakened by coarse summaries while remaining present in bare-earth topography.
items.named_mimic: Road-cut or irrigation-canal bank; terrace risers and landslide scarps are additional controls.
items.differs_from_repo: No actual template search is implemented in this checkout. The legacy fields named amplitude/SNR/relative age are proxies, not Scarplet outputs. Sare and Hilley establish a relevant published method, not novelty or competition benefit for this implementation. Registry-wide uniqueness remains unknown.
items.cost: High: method-faithful template implementation, orientation/age calibration, tile boundaries, visible-fault-only feature construction, feature-alone canaries, blocked validation, and registry checks.
items.expected_gain: High qualitative prior for slope-tolerant scarp signatures; size and direction are unmeasured. No score projection.
items.data_status: Blocked by the same missing authorized DEM tiles, cache, mask, and exact grid/reference files as LIDAR-01 (S04, S05, S07).
items.validation: NOT RUN. Evaluate this as an ablation against a mass-matched baseline on the frozen spatial holdout before combining it with line channels.
items.implementation_status: NOT RUN. Its channel set is a subset of the H67-1 composition.

items.title: Signed, scale-persistent Steger ridge/valley and Frangi Hessian channels alone
items.layers: The same native DEM and shared cache; scale-normalized Hessian structure, signed Steger ridge/valley responses, sub-pixel line locations, and orientation at 2–20 m; summarize response strength, sign, scale persistence, and orientation coherence at 100 m.
items.signature: A paired, sign-consistent linear relief break persists at adjacent scales and traces a coherent line rather than appearing as an isolated edge at one scale.
items.why_off_catalogue: Native-resolution ridge/valley localization may preserve short or low-relief scarps that a single-scale or 100 m response misses.
items.named_mimic: Natural stream-bank line. Roads, field edges, terrace breaks, and DEM seams are additional controls.
items.differs_from_repo: No footprint-wide Steger sub-pixel or Frangi scale sweep is present. These established line operators are not novel by themselves; owner-maintained sibling reports describe LiDAR thinning and scarp consensus. A complete registry is needed to test the exact signed/persistence surface for duplication or lane drift.
items.cost: High: scale normalization, polarity/sign rules, edge suppression, tile seams, response calibration, feature-alone leakage tests, and full uniqueness/holdout gates.
items.expected_gain: Moderate qualitative prior with substantial non-fault mimic risk; sign and size are unknown. No DTI projection.
items.data_status: Blocked by missing authorized DEM/cache; public availability of USGS 3DEP does not prove exact tile coverage or compatibility (S05, S07, S08).
items.validation: NOT RUN. Test each signed response alone before any combination; apply the AUC leakage stop and same-fold mass-matched comparison.
items.implementation_status: PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED: the signed, scale-persistent line channels exist (part_tensor_*, persistence behind the hedge component).

items.title: Ordered cross-profile polarity and along-strike continuity
items.layers: The same native DEM and verified existing mask; sampled cross-profiles recording paired slope breaks, polarity, width, local relief, orientation, and along-strike persistence over 2–20 m; aggregate profile fractions and continuity to 100 m.
items.signature: Repeated profiles with consistent step polarity and crest/toe ordering along a trace, rather than one isolated edge or a chain of unrelated line responses.
items.why_off_catalogue: A real fault scarp may be below regional-map inclusion criteria but retain repeated, similarly oriented cross-profile geometry along a trace.
items.named_mimic: Fluvial terrace edge; road/canal banks and landslide headscarps can also create ordered breaks.
items.differs_from_repo: This is a proposed profile-order/continuity ablation inside the same LiDAR lane, not evidence of a separate lane. Existing owner reports describe scarp channels/consensus, and complete registry surfaces are not available; uniqueness is unverified.
items.cost: Medium-high: profile extraction is tractable, but polarity handling, continuity thresholds, mimic controls, aggregation, ablation, holdout, and registry checks remain necessary.
items.expected_gain: Lower qualitative prior than the first three; may improve precision if ordered profiles separate faults from mimics, but may discard discontinuous real scarps. Unquantified.
items.data_status: Blocked by missing authorized DEM/cache and existing mask; exact coverage/alignment is not established (S05, S07, S08).
items.validation: NOT RUN. Prespecify profile/persistence thresholds, test each feature alone, then use the same segment-blocked holdout and uniqueness gates.
items.implementation_status: NOT RUN. Polarity pairing is now re-ranked as G-03.

items.title: Scarp-sharpness (relative-age) ordering gate on the scarp lane
items.layers: L_ex_max, L_step_max, L_lappos_max, L_lapneg_max, L_cross_max, L_relief, L_coh100, L_strike, L_valid (all present in data/processed/stack.f32)
items.signature: Dimensionless sharpness A = L_ex_max/(L_step_max+eps) and curvature asymmetry (lappos-lapneg)/(lappos+lapneg) per 100 m cell; the AGU 2015 wavelet-template result is that young, gently-dipping scarps show high step response and low diffusion amplitude and are missed by vertical-scarp templates. Transform: per-cell rank, 3x3 smoothing, then gate (multiply) the lane field by A.
items.catches_offcatalogue: The competition catalogue is dominated by long, well-expressed, already-mapped traces. A sharpness gate selects the young and subtle scarps an expert adds to a state map, and demotes the degraded lineaments that are already in the database - the opposite of a habitat-style density model.
items.named_mimic: Fluvial terrace risers and channel cut banks (sharp, single-sided, short); landslide head scarps (sharp but isolated, no along-strike continuity).
items.differs_from_repo: No field in the repository uses an amplitude/sharpness ratio or a relative-age axis at all; previous lanes used L_ex_max and L_step_max directly as amplitude z-scores.
items.external_source: None needed (GeoDAWN 1 m-derived channels already mirrored).
items.expected_gain: highest of the five - it re-weights the existing lane by a physical age discriminator instead of adding new data
items.validation: Falsification only: blocked whole-component holdout must not reject it; certification needs an organizer receipt (IR-67-INSTR-01).
items.data_status: layers present; no new download required

items.title: Along-strike persistence of the scarp lane across three scales
items.signature: Box-mean scarp evidence at 3, 5 and 9 cells (300 m, 500 m, 900 m) combined by a persistence product (geometric mean of the three normalised ranks). A tectonic trace persists at every scale; a cultural edge or a single-cell artefact does not.
items.catches_offcatalogue: Expert-added faults are typically shorter and less continuous than map-scale faults, so a persistence test removes the false positives that dominate a naive scarp-density map, without needing any catalogue habitat prior.
items.named_mimic: Irrigation field boundaries (long, straight, mixed orientation) and rail/road grades.
items.differs_from_repo: The repository's coherence channel L_coh100 is single-scale and the lane parts were never combined into a persistence product; the hedge component uses scale persistence of the structure tensor only.
items.expected_gain: moderate - sharpens precision at roughly constant recall

items.title: Cross-trace polarity pairing against the local dip azimuth
items.layers: L_downface_max, L_upface_max, L_relief, L_strike, det_elev_slope (100 m stack), L_valid
items.signature: Require opposed face directions (up-face and down-face) in adjacent cells whose pairing axis is perpendicular to the dip azimuth from det_elev_slope, i.e. a step whose sense is consistent along strike. Transform: signed dot product of face direction with the gradient azimuth, gated by sign agreement over 3 cells.
items.catches_offcatalogue: A tectonic step has a consistent down-thrown side along its length; that is exactly what a catalogue gap hides (short, low-relief scarps). Single-sided geomorphic edges cannot satisfy the pairing.
items.named_mimic: Pluvial shoreline terraces (paired but concentric, not aligned to a through-going dip azimuth); eolian dune margins.
items.differs_from_repo: No prior field pairs the up-face and down-face channels; they are used separately in the lane parts.
items.expected_gain: moderate - increases precision on the polarity axis, at some recall cost

items.title: Scarp lane x potassium corridor intersection
items.layers: L_ex_max, L_step_max, L_strike, rad_K, rad_U, rad_Th, ext_UK, iso_grav_anom_hg, L_valid
items.signature: Product of the scarp-lane ranks with K-enrichment and gravity-gradient-maximum ranks, then a local maximum along the local strike direction. Hydrothermal alteration along a fault raises K/U and lowers Th/K ratios; a fault with a weak scarp can be caught by its alteration corridor.
items.catches_offcatalogue: Catches faults expressed by alteration or fluid pathways rather than by fresh topography, which is how several Basin-and-Range catalogue gaps look.
items.named_mimic: Playa evaporite potassium and irrigated/fertilised fields (K anomalies without any scarp lane, removed by the product); mining disturbance.
items.differs_from_repo: Radiometrics are used in the repository as supervised classification features only, never as a multiplicative corridor gate on the lane. Named family precedent: GEMSDOE46 scarp-radiometric fusion (owner-reported 0.1589) - kept at rank 4 for that reason.
items.external_source: GeoDAWN airborne radiometrics, USGS ScienceBase item 657e1d85d34e23d3533209f7, DOI 10.5066/P93LGLVQ (already mirrored as rad_* / ext_UK)
items.obtainable: YES (already local; original source unreachable from this sandbox)
items.expected_gain: moderate but uncertain - the named family precedent scored below the incumbent

items.title: Native-resolution Steger/Frangi sub-pixel lines at 2-20 m (the brief's target method)
items.layers: USGS 3DEP native 1 m DEM tiles; GeoDAWN 1 m lidar; 10 m 3DEP DEM for the channel-steepness layers
items.signature: Sub-pixel ridge/valley line position from the Hessian eigenvector (Steger) and multiscale vesselness (Frangi) on a slope-detrended surface, aggregated to 100 m as scarp-pixel fraction, SNR-weighted amplitude, orientation coherence and dominant strike.
items.catches_offcatalogue: It resolves 2-20 m steps that no 100 m aggregate can see - the actual scale of the scarps experts identify in lidar.
items.named_mimic: Dirt roads, canals and field edges, which is why the cultural mask is mandatory (IR-67-MASK-01).
items.differs_from_repo: Everything in the repository runs at the 100 m cell scale; this is the only truly native-resolution option.
items.external_source: USGS 3DEP (https://www.usgs.gov/3d-elevation-program) 1 m DEM; GeoDAWN sciencebase item 657e1d85d34e23d3533209f7
items.obtainable: NO from this sandbox (HTTP 000 to all tile hosts); requires an authorised environment
items.expected_gain: unknown but potentially the largest - it is the only option that changes the underlying data scale
items.validation: Requires the full pre-registered protocol plus a cultural mask before it may be ranked above G-01.

items.title: Catalogue-flank habitat x scarp-channel gate (flank_scgate)
items.layers: 1 m-derived step_max, coh100, dip-sense persistence (downface/upface over a 3 km window); catalogue distance ring 200-800 m (geometry prior only); TIGER road veto; BLM claim soft penalty.
items.signature: A native slope-break with coherent dip sense inside a 200-800 m ring around the mapped trace: the sibling/stepover population that expert panels add to public catalogues.
items.why_off_catalogue: Expert-added faults are structurally related to known faults (parallel families, stepovers) yet absent from the public database; the ring selects that geometry while the scarp gate demands physical evidence.
items.named_mimic: Range-front scarp parallel to a mapped fault; road cuts along basin margins.
items.differs_from_repo: Incumbent family uses the flank geometry WITHOUT a native scarp-evidence gate; prior scarp rasters use the scarp evidence WITHOUT the flank geometry. The conjunction is new to the registry.
items.expected_gain: Highest qualitative prior (builds on the incumbent's demonstrably working geometry). Not a DTI projection.
items.cost: Low (feature engineering on the cached stack).
items.validation: MEASURED 2026-10-12: canary AUC 0.4949 (sub-chance mean; folds 0.35-0.63). Not emitted - weakest composite. No holdout DTI claimed.
items.data_status: Implemented on hash-pinned 1 m-derived stack + pinned cultural layers.

items.title: Young-scarp band (young_scarp): 0.3-3 m steps in gentle relief with crest-toe sharpness
items.layers: 1 m-derived step_max (height = step x 10 m), lapneg_max x lappos_max (sharpness), coh100, dip-sense persistence, L_relief <= p75 band; cultural veto.
items.signature: The 'easiest to miss' recent normal-fault band: small asymmetric steps (0.3-3 m) with a sharp crest-concavity toe pair in gentle relief, coherent along strike.
items.why_off_catalogue: State maps digitize mapped, older, larger faults; young (<~50 ka) scarps of the 1-3 m class are the population most likely absent from the public database and present in the hidden set.
items.named_mimic: Terrace risers and irrigation canals of the same amplitude; young alluvial-fan margins.
items.differs_from_repo: H66-2 used sharpness inside a 3-term concordance without the young-band amplitude/relief selection; H66-2 was judged negative on transfer. The explicit band + dip-sense persistence term is new.
items.expected_gain: Second prior: physically targeted at the unmapped population. Not a DTI projection.
items.validation: MEASURED 2026-10-12: canary AUC 0.4895. Not emitted (weaker than the h52 channel). No holdout DTI claimed.

items.title: Along-strike scarp persistence (persistence): 2 km / 5 km corridor line-continuity
items.layers: 1 m-derived ex_max walked +/- 2 and 5 km along the local strike field; corridor amplitude mean and fraction of samples above domain p90; coh100; cultural veto.
items.signature: km-scale linear persistence of scarp amplitude - the classic fault discriminator against isolated steps (channels, mines, cuts).
items.why_off_catalogue: Long subtle scarps that outrun mapping campaigns are prime expert-add candidates.
items.named_mimic: Terrace risers and paleo-shorelines are equally persistent - the named mimic this candidate is most exposed to.
items.differs_from_repo: No registry raster scores along-strike corridor persistence on the 1 m-derived amplitude field.
items.expected_gain: Third prior; strong mimic exposure lowers the net expectation. Not a DTI projection.
items.cost: Medium (directional walks, 100 m steps over the full grid).
items.validation: MEASURED 2026-10-12: canary AUC 0.5322 (folds 0.36-0.70; no fold above 0.71). Not emitted after E1 (weaker than the h52 channel; E2/E3 budget spent on the strongest in-lane surface). No holdout DTI claimed.

items.title: Strike bimodality / X-junction (bimodal_x): two coherent scarp directions >= 20 deg apart within 5 km
items.layers: 36-bin doubled-angle histogram of strike weighted by step_max over a 5 km disc; top-1 share, top-2 share and separation; cultural veto.
items.signature: Relay/stepover X-junctions: secondary slip directions that public maps rarely digitize where two fault trends cross.
items.why_off_catalogue: Secondary slip zones and stepover relays are systematically under-mapped in state compilations.
items.named_mimic: Joint-set interference in rock outcrops (structural, not fault-scarp); road-grid intersections.
items.differs_from_repo: New; no registry raster uses local strike bimodality.
items.expected_gain: Fourth prior; low evidence density at the 100 m grid. Not a DTI projection.
items.validation: MEASURED 2026-10-12: canary AUC 0.5362 (folds 0.37-0.67). Not emitted (E1). No holdout DTI claimed.

items.title: Scarp x aeromagnetic offset coupling (mag_offset)
items.layers: step_max x smoothed-TMI gradient magnitude, with the gradient crossing the scarp strike near 90 deg (|sin(az - strike)|); dip-sense persistence; cultural veto.
items.signature: A scarp that displaced a magnetic body: a sharp ~100-500 m magnetic offset aligned with the slope-break trace.
items.why_off_catalogue: Subtle recent faults that offset a magnetic contact but were never mapped.
items.named_mimic: Contact magnetism along dikes/lithology boundaries; magnetic mapping artifacts.
items.differs_from_repo: r11f-scarp-radiometric-fusion (0.1589 owner-reported) used radiometrics; the magnetic-offset angular coupling is a different measurement, but lane-drift risk against the scarp-geophysics family is the reason it ranked last.
items.expected_gain: Fifth prior (highest lane-drift risk). Not a DTI projection.
items.validation: MEASURED 2026-10-12: canary AUC 0.5159. Not emitted (E1). No holdout DTI claimed.
items.data_status: Implemented on the pinned stack + competition TMI bands.

items.title: Mapping-gap / catalogue-distance prior
items.signature: A hard exclusion of emission within 200 m of any mapped fault, ramping to full credit at 600 m.
items.why_it_catches_an_unmapped_fault: The scored truth is explicitly disjoint from the public database, so mass placed on or beside a mapped fault cannot earn kernel credit but still pays the alpha = 0.2 false-positive cost. Byte-verified: h33-2-b2 = d28 minus exactly the 6,436 dots within 200 m of the catalogue, 0.2600 -> 0.2778 owner-reported.
items.difference_from_this_repo: No prior H66 artifact models the catalogue-distance prior; the inherited emission only deleted dots within 200 m as a post-hoc filter.
items.named_mimic: A genuinely new splay or along-strike continuation of a mapped fault would be suppressed by this prior; the dose response cannot distinguish that from a mapping gap.
items.expected_dti_improvement: largest of the three (the only byte-verified effect)
items.status: implemented and used in the candidate; NOT validated by any local instrument

items.title: Diffused-scarp template inversion (scarplet physics)
layers: lidar_scarp_features_u8 ex_max (2 m slope excess over the 30 m regional slope)
lapneg_max / lappos_max (6 m LoG of the 50 m band-passed surface)
items.signature: a_hat = 1.5203 S^2/C and kappa*t_hat = 1.5203^2 a_hat^2/(4 pi S^2) from the analytic erf-scarp diffusion profile.
items.why_it_catches_an_unmapped_fault: A scarp that has diffused keeps an antisymmetric crest-convexity/toe-concavity pair and a recoverable height/age pair long after its amplitude has dropped below what a 100 m stack or an amplitude threshold can see.
items.difference_from_this_repo: channels66.py only formed heuristic ratios (mean/max, slope ratio, robust z); it never inverted the diffusion model.
items.named_mimic: Fluvial terrace riser (identical curvature dipole and strike coherence).
items.status: implemented; channels built; no measurable gain on instrument N

Items G-01..G-05 are new geological hypotheses added 2026-10-12, ranked by qualitative expected improvement per unit implementation cost. No expected gain is a DTI projection, and no internal instrument can certify a gain (IR-67-INSTR-01, IR-67-CONFOUND-01).
